features.description: Ledger writer stamps a nullable canonical_repo {path_key, path_display, durable_checkout, origin_key?} at write time, alongside the observed `repo`, resolving via the C3 three-case rule. ALGORITHM (pinned): canonical_root = run `git -C <observed_root> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`; the returned common-dir points at the MAIN worktree's git dir for both a main checkout and a linked worktree; canonical_root = the parent dir of that common-dir when it ends in `/.git` (a linked-worktree `.git` FILE still resolves the common-dir to the main repo, so this collapses worktrees to their main checkout); if the common-dir does not end in `.git` (bare repo) or no working tree exists, treat as unresolved. worktrees.py only COMPARES common-dirs (binding_health, line ~259) and does NOT return the main-checkout path, so add a new small helper rather than reusing it. CASES (C3): (1) durable+git -> canonical=main-checkout root, durable_checkout=true; (2) durable+non-git (rev-parse fails) -> canonical=self (observed root), durable_checkout=true; (3) temp-observed -> 3a resolves to a durable canonical root => canonical=that root, durable_checkout=true; 3b resolution fails OR canonical root is itself temp => NO canonical_repo stamped (field absent). durable_checkout is a property of the CANONICAL repo (is it non-temp/on-disk-stable), never of the observed path. A temp path is never stamped as canonical and is never self-canonicalized. Records read by older code without the field must continue to load.
steps: Read invocation_ledger.py (path_key/make_path_pair, _detect_repo_root, _detect_branch, start_recording base dict, _bucket_key, compaction/_BUCKET_KEY_FIELDS) and worktrees.py (~line 259, binding_health: it COMPARES common-dirs, does not return the main checkout path) before any change.

Add canonicalize_repo(observed_root) -> {canonical_root|None, origin_url|None, durable_checkout} implementing the pinned algorithm: single `git -C <root> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` probe, derive canonical_root = parent of common-dir ending in `/.git`; classify into the three C3 cases using a temp-prefix test (/tmp, /private/tmp, /var/folders) on BOTH the observed root and the resolved canonical root. Case 3b returns canonical_root=None. No shelling beyond the one probe (+ optional one `remote get-url origin`).

In start_recording, when canonical_root is not None stamp canonical_repo = make_path_pair(canonical_root) plus durable_checkout and optional origin_key (hash of the normalized origin URL; never the raw URL — C1). When canonical_root is None (case 3b), omit canonical_repo entirely. Leave the observed `repo` and repo.path_key untouched (C2).
Ensure _bucket_key and conflict/locality logic continue to key on repo.path_key, NOT canonical_repo_key (C2). Add a regression test asserting bucket behavior is unchanged.

Extend compaction-preserved fields so canonical_repo survives compact_ledger (else grouping breaks post-compaction) and compacted rows carry observed_count = sum of collapsed record observed_count values, with legacy/no-field records counting as 1. If a compaction bucket mixes canonical-bearing and non-canonical rows, or mixes different canonical_repo.path_key values, preserve the existing observed bucket but omit canonical_repo, set canonical_compaction_conflict=true, and do not carry a canonical observed_count.
Confirm no raw home path or raw origin URL is persisted: extend/verify the no-secret-shape assertion over the new fields (C1).

Tests, one per C3 case: (1) durable git checkout -> canonical=self-root, durable=true; (1) linked worktree of a durable repo -> canonical=main-checkout root, durable=true; (2) durable non-git dir -> canonical=self, durable=true; (3a) temp worktree of a durable repo -> canonical=durable main, durable=true; (3b) temp dir with failed/temp resolution -> NO canonical_repo field; plus legacy record without canonical_repo still loads; bucket-key regression; no-secret-shape over new fields.
features.acceptance: (1) When resolvable to a durable root, records carry canonical_repo {path_key, path_display, durable_checkout=true, origin_key?}, surviving compaction; when unresolvable from a temp path (C3 case 3b) the field is absent, never a temp canonical. (2) repo.path_key is unchanged and still drives bucket/conflict/locality logic, proven by a regression test (C2). (3) compact_ledger usage-count invariant, proven by a before/after fixture: in a fixture of duplicate records, legacy/no-field rows count as 1 and rows carrying observed_count sum correctly; compacted output preserves the same derive_buckets grouping plus the summed observed_count, and canonical_repo survives compaction; F003 reads the identical observed_count for a canonical repo before and after compaction (a before==after assertion, not merely 'a count test exists'). (4) Mixed-attribution compaction is fail-closed and tested: a bucket containing both canonical-bearing and legacy/non-canonical rows, or multiple canonical keys, emits canonical_compaction_conflict=true, omits canonical_repo, carries no canonical observed_count, and F003 ignores it so observed_count is neither inflated nor dropped silently. (5) durable_checkout describes the canonical repo; a temp worktree of a durable repo yields durable_checkout=true (C2/C3-3a), and a temp path is never self-canonicalized (C3). (6) No raw home path or raw origin URL is persisted anywhere (C1). (7) Records written before this feature still load; tests cover all three C3 cases, legacy-record, bucket-regression, compaction count invariance, mixed-attribution compaction conflict, and no-secret-shape.

features.description: Canonical backfill evidence contract. Defines the exact C4 evidence shape so ambiguity detection is deterministic before the F002 engine consumes the file.
steps: Define the C4 evidence contract exactly as plan.md specifies: version 1.0, canonical repo map keyed by canonical path key, and observation-key map whose values are lists of canonical path keys.

Validate allowed canonical repo fields, required field presence, exact value types, and no-secret shape before F002 can copy any field: path_key and path_display are strings, durable_checkout is boolean, optional observed_under_temp_prefix is boolean, and optional origin_key is a hash-shaped string accepted by the shared no-secret-shape assertion, never a raw URL.

Reject unknown fields, missing required fields, wrong value types, raw-secret-shaped values, unknown canonical references, non-list observation mappings, empty mapping lists, and multi-key mapping lists as malformed or ambiguous.

Tests cover valid evidence, missing required top-level keys, wrong version, unknown canonical key, mismatched path key, non-list mapping, zero mappings, multiple mappings, unknown canonical fields, missing required fields, wrong value types, raw origin URL / no-secret-shape failure, and optional hash-shaped origin/temp-observed fields.
features.acceptance: (1) The C4 evidence contract is implemented and tested: required top-level keys, version 1.0, canonical repo map keyed by canonical path key, observation-key map with list values, only allowed canonical repo fields, required field presence, exact value types, and no-secret-shape validation before any field can be copied. (2) Malformed or ambiguous evidence is classified deterministically: missing keys, wrong version, unknown canonical references, mismatched path keys, unknown fields, missing required fields, wrong value types, raw-secret-shaped values, non-list values, zero mappings, and multiple mappings. (3) Optional origin and temp-observed fields are accepted only in the allowed canonical repo shape; origin_key must be hash-shaped and is rejected if it looks like a raw origin URL.

features.description: One-time, idempotent canonical backfill engine over historical invocations.jsonl using operator-local evidence captured while the temp worktrees still exist. It consumes the F006 evidence contract and stamps canonical_repo onto matching historical records that lack it. The evidence file is local operator evidence and is NOT committed (C4). The backfill is re-runnable without duplicate mutation, and refuses ambiguous mappings using the deterministic C4 evidence validation matrix: absent observation key, unknown canonical key, missing required field, wrong value type, raw-secret-shaped value, path_key mismatch, non-reconstructable scrub token, failed path-key confirmation, reconstructed temp canonical path, or evidence claiming durable_checkout=true for a temp canonical path all SKIP + report reason, never guessed. origin_key is copied only from the single confirmed canonical evidence object after F006 proves it is hash-shaped and not a raw URL. Any written canonical_repo.path_display is recomputed through make_path_pair/shared scrubber; raw home-path evidence is normalized to <home> before write, never copied through.
steps: Load and validate evidence through the F006 contract; refuse malformed/missing files with a clear message.

Implement C4 confirmation as a pure evidence-matrix check: CONFIRMED iff record.repo.path_key resolves through the F006 mapping to exactly one canonical entry, path_display is reconstructable by the C1 home-token or literal-display rules, recomputing make_path_pair from the reconstructed local path yields the same path_key, the reconstructed canonical path is not under /tmp, /private/tmp, or /var/folders, and the display to be written is the recomputed scrubbed display. Copy origin_key only from that single confirmed canonical entry; do not implement a separate origin_key conflict cell.

Implement an idempotent pass: for each ledger record lacking canonical_repo, stamp canonical_repo {path_key, path_display, durable_checkout, origin_key?} only when the evidence-matrix check returns CONFIRMED; if evidence provides a literal absolute path under Path.home(), normalize the written path_display to the recomputed <home>-scrubbed value; if the record already has canonical_repo, skip (idempotence).

Refuse ambiguous/unconfirmable mappings: absent observation key, multiple canonical keys, malformed canonical_repo field, missing required field, wrong value type, raw-secret-shaped value, path_key mismatch, non-reconstructable scrub token, failed path-key confirmation, reconstructed canonical path under a temp prefix, or durable_checkout=true claimed for a temp canonical path leaves the record untouched and adds it to a reported `skipped` list with reason (C4).
Never write a temp-prefix path as a canonical recommendation source; durable_checkout is copied from the evidence entry (C3).

Write the updated ledger atomically (temp-file + rename) while holding the same ledger lock used by the live invocation writer across the full read/validate/write/rename critical section; preserve record order and all existing fields; do not parse or alter the command field (C6).
Add the repo-local guard for overridden DONTPANIC_HOME: .gitignore ignores `.dontpanic/canonical-backfill-evidence.json`, and a test/doc check proves the evidence file is never tracked.

Tests: idempotent re-run is a no-op; unambiguous match stamps correctly; literal home path evidence writes <home>-scrubbed display; ambiguous/absent keys are skipped+reported; malformed evidence refuses cleanly; missing required fields, wrong types, and raw origin URL/no-secret-shape failures skip before copy; non-reconstructable scrub token skips; path_key mismatch skips; origin_key is copied from the single confirmed canonical entry only after hash-shape validation; reconstructed temp canonical path skips even when durable_checkout=true; record order + other fields preserved; concurrent append under the writer lock is serialized or the backfill refuses without replacing the ledger; the 51-record fixture (p2a/p2-lock/main) collapses to one canonical repo key; evidence-file ignore/commit guard is covered.
features.acceptance: (1) The backfill engine consumes the F006 evidence contract and stamps canonical_repo onto matching historical records idempotently (re-run is a no-op), and any written path_display is the recomputed scrubbed display; literal evidence under the operator home is normalized to <home> and never copied through raw. (2) The deterministic C4 evidence matrix is implemented and tested: absent key, missing required field, wrong value type, raw-secret-shaped value, path_key mismatch, non-reconstructable scrub token, failed path-key confirmation, reconstructed temp canonical path, and durable_checkout=true claimed for a temp canonical path are refused and reported, never guessed; origin_key is copied only from the single confirmed canonical evidence object after hash-shape/no-secret validation. (3) Backfill write mode holds the same ledger lock as the live writer across read/validate/write/temp-file/rename; a concurrent append is serialized into the rewritten ledger or the backfill fails without replacement, never lost. (4) The evidence file is local-only and not committed, enforced by repo-local ignore plus commit-guard test/doc check. (5) The command field is never parsed (C6). (6) A fixture mirroring the 51 records collapses the three observed paths to one canonical repo key; ledger record order and unrelated fields are preserved.

features.description: Backfill operator entrypoint for the F002 engine. Implements the C4-pinned surface, default path resolution, status behavior, and stable report schema so the one-time migration is operator-testable without changing the engine contract.
steps: Implement the C4-pinned backfill entrypoint exactly as specified in plan.md, including preview/write modes and explicit ledger/evidence path overrides.
Resolve default ledger and evidence paths through the same global-config home logic used by the ledger writer.

In write mode, acquire the same ledger lock used by live invocation appends and hold it across the F002 read/validate/write/temp-file/rename sequence; if the lock/replace sequence cannot guarantee no lost append, fail with the C4 write-failure code without replacing the ledger.
Return status per C4: completed reports use the success code even when rows are skipped; usage/input/write failures use the failure code.
Render the stable report schema from C4 with scrubbed ledger/evidence paths: would_stamp, would_skip, already_stamped, and stamped are counts; skipped is the detail list of {path_key, reason} rows.

Tests: default path resolution honors the configured home; explicit ledger/evidence overrides are used; preview mode does not write; concurrent append is not lost during write mode; status behavior and report schema are covered; negative hook guard proves the command does not install, modify, remove, chain, read, or depend on git hooks.
features.acceptance: (1) The C4-pinned backfill entrypoint consumes default global-config evidence/ledger paths or explicit overrides, supports preview and write modes, reports with the stable schema, and follows the C4 status contract. (2) Write mode coordinates with the live writer lock for the full critical section and tests prove a concurrent append is serialized or the backfill refuses without replacing the ledger. (3) Reported ledger/evidence paths are scrubbed. (4) Tests cover configured-home defaults, explicit path overrides, no-write preview behavior, status behavior, report schema, and the C7 negative hook guard.

features.description: Ledger adapter + registry adapter + pure registry-vs-observed reconciliation function (no presentation layer, no output formatting). observed_canonical_from_ledger reads invocations.jsonl into observed_canonical rows by skipping records without canonical_repo or with canonical_compaction_conflict=true, summing observed_count (legacy/no-field rows count as 1) and max last_seen by canonical_repo.path_key, preserving scrubbed path_display and durable_checkout, and never reading record.command. registered_canonical_from_registry pre-enriches registry rows using F001 canonicalization/path checks into {name, active, path_display, canonical_repo_key?, path_exists, canonicalization_status, registry_path_key?}. reconcile(registered_canonical, observed_canonical, now, policy) is pure: it joins those enriched inputs and returns {used_unregistered, registered_active, registered_stale, registered_path_missing, registered_unresolved}. Canonical rows are keyed on canonical_repo_key; registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved rows use registry_name + registry_path_key and have canonical_repo_key=null. Applies the pinned C5 policy defaults and registered active/stale truth table (window_days=14, min_count=2, timestamp=last_seen, inclusive boundaries), durability-gates temp paths out of recommendations (C3), dedupes to one row per canonical_repo_key, derives safe suggested_name values for unregistered candidates, and uses only structured metadata and timestamps (C6).
steps: Implement observed_canonical_from_ledger(records) as the explicit IO adapter contract: read invocation records; skip records without canonical_repo, with canonical_repo.durable_checkout != true, or with canonical_compaction_conflict=true; aggregate by canonical_repo.path_key; sum record.observed_count defaulting to 1 for legacy/no-field rows; take max last_seen; preserve scrubbed path_display and origin_key/durable_checkout; never read record.command.

Implement registered_canonical_from_registry(entries) as the registry-side IO adapter: for each ProjectEntry, check path existence, compute canonical_repo_key/path_display via the same canonicalization as F001 when path exists, and emit {name, active, path_display, canonical_repo_key?, path_exists, canonicalization_status, registry_path_key?}. Missing paths emit path_exists=false, canonical_repo_key=null, canonicalization_status=missing, and registry_path_key=sha256(normalized stored registry path)[:16]. Existing paths whose canonicalization fails emit path_exists=true, canonical_repo_key=null, canonicalization_status=unresolved, and the same registry_path_key fallback.

Implement reconcile(registered_canonical, observed_canonical, now, policy) as a pure function returning the five-state projection; used_unregistered/registered_active/registered_stale rows are keyed by canonical_repo_key, while registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved rows are keyed by registry_name + registry_path_key with canonical_repo_key=null. It never performs filesystem or git probes.

Apply the decay/threshold policy (C5): defaults are window_days=14, min_count=2, timestamp field=last_seen, used_unregistered passes when observed_count >= min_count and last_seen >= now - window_days (inclusive); missing/invalid last_seen fails closed. Apply the registered-row truth table: missing path -> registered_path_missing; existing path with failed canonicalization -> registered_unresolved; active=false -> no active/stale row; registered existing non-inactive canonicalized path with no observed row or failed threshold/invalid timestamp -> registered_stale; registered existing non-inactive canonicalized path passing both inclusive thresholds -> registered_active. Make policy overridable by the F004 command.

Durability-gate (C3): exclude any candidate whose canonical resolution is non-durable / temp-prefixed from used_unregistered; such usage contributes only to a durable canonical repo when one is resolvable.
Dedupe candidates to one row per canonical_repo_key (the p2a/p2-lock/main case yields a single `dontpanic` candidate), summing observed_count and taking max last_seen.

Derive suggested_name for used_unregistered rows from scrubbed path_display basename: lowercase, replace non-[a-z0-9-] with hyphen, collapse/trim hyphens, default to `project`, enforce the project-name regex, and append -<canonical_repo_key[:8]> on collision while staying within 64 chars.
Metadata-only (C6): the function reads only repo/canonical_repo metadata + timestamps, never record.command.

Tests: ledger adapter skips missing canonical_repo and canonical_compaction_conflict rows; ledger adapter aggregates observed_count defaulting legacy rows to 1 plus max last_seen by canonical_repo.path_key; mixed-attribution compacted rows do not inflate or drop a canonical observed_count; ledger adapter preserves scrubbed display; ledger adapter never reads command (secret-shaped command fixture); registry adapter emits registry_path_key and canonical_repo_key=null for missing and unresolved registered paths and canonical keys for existing canonicalized paths; reconcile has no filesystem/git IO; empty-registry/zero-observed yields empty arrays; default threshold filters low-count/old/repos at inclusive boundaries and is stable after compacted observed_count rows; registered active/stale truth-table cells are tested for absent observed row, invalid/missing last_seen, low count, old last_seen, inactive entry, unresolved canonicalization, and passing thresholds; temp-prefix usage never appears as used_unregistered; suggested_name derivation/collision/hash suffix is tested; isolated fixture registry with the target repo absent yields one used_unregistered candidate; D010-like fixture registry with the target repo present yields registered_active; registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved classification/key shapes are tested.
features.acceptance: (1) observed_canonical_from_ledger() is implemented and tested as the explicit ledger adapter: records without canonical_repo or with canonical_compaction_conflict=true are skipped, rows aggregate observed_count by canonical_repo.path_key with legacy/no-field rows counting as 1, scrubbed path_display is preserved, durable_checkout is carried, max last_seen is preserved, and record.command is never read. (2) registered_canonical_from_registry() is implemented and tested as the registry adapter: existing paths are canonicalized before pure reconcile; missing and unresolved paths emit canonical_repo_key=null, registry_path_key=sha256(normalized stored registry path)[:16], canonicalization_status, and scrubbed path_display. (3) reconcile() returns {used_unregistered, registered_active, registered_stale, registered_path_missing, registered_unresolved}; canonical rows are keyed on canonical_repo_key, registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved rows are keyed by registry_name + registry_path_key with canonical_repo_key=null; reconcile has no filesystem/git IO and zero-state yields empty arrays. (4) C5 defaults and registered-row truth table are pinned and tested: window_days=14, min_count=2, timestamp=last_seen, inclusive observed_count >= min_count and last_seen >= now-window_days; missing path -> registered_path_missing; unresolved canonicalization -> registered_unresolved; inactive -> no active/stale row; existing canonicalized registered path with absent/invalid/stale/low-count observed row -> registered_stale; existing canonicalized registered path passing both thresholds -> registered_active. (5) Mixed-attribution compacted rows marked canonical_compaction_conflict do not inflate or drop canonical observed_count. (6) suggested_name derivation for used_unregistered rows is deterministic, project-name-regex safe, collision-safe with canonical_repo_key hash suffix, and JSON-safe. (7) Temp-prefix / non-durable usage never appears as used_unregistered (C3); isolated/D010-like fixtures produce used_unregistered vs registered_active; registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved key shapes are tested; adapters/reconcile never read command (C6).

features.description: `dontpanic projects discover [--json]` CLI wrapping the F003 adapters + reconcile function. Loads the registry and invocation ledger, builds observed_canonical and registered_canonical, calls reconcile, and renders JSON and concise human output. It wires C5 defaults (window_days=14, min_count=2, timestamp=last_seen, inclusive boundaries) and overrides `--window-days` / `--min-count`. Privacy boundary (C1): --json emits canonical_repo_key + scrubbed path_display + counts/recency + suggestion status + suggested_name only, never a reconstructed raw add path. registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved JSON rows carry canonical_repo_key=null and registry_name + registry_path_key. Default human output may print a locally reconstructed `dontpanic projects add <suggested_name> <path>` command using the three C1 rules. No raw path is ever persisted or serialized.
steps: Add the `discover` subcommand to the existing `dontpanic projects` CLI; it loads ledger + registry, builds observed_canonical and registered_canonical via F003 adapters, applies C5 defaults, accepts `--window-days` and `--min-count` overrides, and emits --json with scrubbed display + keys + counts/recency + suggestion status only; default prints a concise human summary of used_unregistered + stale + path_missing.

Pin the render matrix: JSON never serializes reconstructed raw add paths; human output may reconstruct the add-command path operator-locally per C1 rules (a) home-token -> Path.home() substitution, (b) literal -> verbatim, (c) non-reconstructable scrub token -> literal `<path>` placeholder + needs-manual-path flag. Never persist or read a raw absolute path; never fabricate one.
Assert no raw home path appears anywhere in the --json output (reuse the no-secret-shape assertion).
Never touch record.command in the CLI path either (C6).

Tests: --json shape matches the reconcile contract and contains no reconstructed raw add path; registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved JSON carry registry_name + registry_path_key and canonical_repo_key=null; JSON includes safe suggested_name for used_unregistered rows; CLI default policy uses window_days=14/min_count=2/last_seen inclusive boundaries and overrides pass through; JSON reflects the C5 registered active/stale truth table for inactive, missing path, unresolved canonicalization, absent observed row, invalid timestamp, low count, stale recency, and passing thresholds; human output lists candidates and may include reconstructed commands with suggested_name; no raw home path in JSON; isolated fixture registry with DontPanic absent yields one used_unregistered suggestion; D010-like fixture registry with DontPanic registered yields registered_active, not used_unregistered; a home-display candidate yields a home-substituted command only in human output; a canonical path OUTSIDE $HOME yields a verbatim-literal human command; a non-reconstructable display yields the placeholder `<path>` command + needs-manual-path; empty-state serializes cleanly; negative hook guard proves the command does not install, modify, remove, chain, read, or depend on git hooks.
features.acceptance: (1) `dontpanic projects discover --json` serializes the F003 reconcile projection after building both observed_canonical and registered_canonical; default human output is concise; empty-state serializes to empty arrays without error. (2) The command supplies the C5 default values and configured CLI overrides to F003 reconcile inputs; F003 owns policy correctness and the active/stale truth-table tests. (3) JSON output contains canonical_repo_key + scrubbed display + counts/recency + suggestion status + suggested_name only; no raw home path and no reconstructed add-command path appear in JSON (C1); registered_path_missing and registered_unresolved JSON rows carry canonical_repo_key=null plus registry_name and registry_path_key, not a fake canonical key. (4) Default human output reconstructs the add-command path operator-locally using suggested_name and the three C1 path rules. (5) The CLI path never parses record.command (C6), never installs/modifies/removes/chains/reads/depends on git hooks (C7), and the isolated/D010-like fixtures produce used_unregistered vs registered_active respectively.
